title: A gate that could not reach a verdict says so, and names what failed
desiredOutcome: run-test-gate grades a step that never produced a verdict - a shell 127, a jest worker killed by a signal, vitest finding no test files - as could-not-run rather than red; a jest failed-to-run names its suite and signal in failing and in the evidence row; a reused verdict's first line carries how to re-measure; a cleared task gate is empty at task scope as the command docs promise, and a gate borrowed from the phase says so on its verdict; a task gate that runs far more than the task declares is reported; and the validator names a comma-joined gate entry and a running phase with no gate or no outcome

tasks.title: run-test-gate grades a no-verdict exit as could-not-run, names a jest failed-to-run's suite and signal, and says whose gate ran
tasks.description: Field reports on 3.0.1, reproduced at HEAD: (1) a gate entry that is not a command exits 127 and is graded RED; files_named reads /bin/sh from the shell's diagnostic as a printed path and produces a false NO OVERLAP. (2) a jest worker killed by SIGSEGV records failing ['Test suite failed to run'] with no suite and no signal, is graded failed, and is then REUSED on the same tree with the --no-reuse hint on the fifth line. (3) vitest's 'No test files found' is graded RED. One rule in observed_step: a non-zero exit with no end-of-run report and a recognised could-not-run signature is could-not-run (reached_a_verdict stays the guard for runners whose exit is a count); the jest reader pairs each failed-to-run heading with its FAIL path and first reason line; all-failed-to-run-with-signal is could-not-run with signal and a signalBasis naming jest's report; overlap asked only of steps that reached a verdict; the reuse banner's first line names --no-reuse. (4) a task whose gate was cleared: gateBasis cleared resolves EMPTY at task scope (commands/task.md already promises it; execute-task.md changes with it), an absent gate keeps the phase fallback, and the preamble names both ids and a 'graded by' line follows the banner without changing the GATE RED/GREEN literal. (5) under --task, coverage reports breadth when the run names suite paths the task does not declare - both counts, never a refusal.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a step exiting 127 with no end-of-run report is graded failed (GATE RED) instead of could-not-run

outcome.technical: no_verdict_signature and jest_worker_signal grade no-verdict exits could-not-run; the jest reader names suite and signal; cleared task gates are empty; the preamble and graded-by line name whose gate ran.
outcome.descriptive: A gate that could not run says so and names the cause, instead of reading as a red.

tasks.title: The validator names a comma-joined gate entry, and a running phase with an empty gate or no desiredOutcome
tasks.description: Additive warnings only (validation stays additive): an entry in testGate or tests.gate that is not a buildCommands key, contains a comma, and whose every comma-part IS a key names the split spelling; a non-terminal phase with a blank or missing desiredOutcome; an in_progress phase (derived) with an empty testGate. The empty gate stays a designed state, so never a refusal.
